| `migrax.metrics.enabled` | `true` | Micrometer metrics of the migrations, when the application has a `MeterRegistry` ([Metrics and tracing](../guides/observability.md)) |
| `migrax.tracing.enabled` | `true` | OpenTelemetry spans of the migrations, when the application has an `OpenTelemetry` |
| `migrax.schemas` | | Schemas to migrate one after another |

!!! note "Native executables"

    Quarkus lists the migrations while it builds the application, because a native executable
    can't look through its own files. Set `migrax.locations` and `migrax.java-package` before
    the build: in a native executable, a different value at runtime finds no new migrations.
    Migrations outside your application, in a library jar, are found only when that jar has a
    Jandex index.

## Readiness check

With `quarkus-smallrye-health` in the application, Migrax adds a `migrax` readiness check: UP
when every migration is applied and none failed, was edited or is missing, DOWN otherwise,
with the counts as data (`/q/health/ready`).

Without the health extension there is no readiness check, and nothing to configure.


---

Source: https://migrax.org/frameworks/micronaut/

# Micronaut

Micronaut 4 and 5 are supported.

## What you need

Migrax comes in two parts, and most projects use both:

| Part | What it's for | How you get it |
|---|---|---|
| A tool for your terminal | Writing migrations from your entities (`generate`) and looking after them: `status`, `lint`, `verify`, `rollback` and the other commands | The Maven plugin, the Gradle plugin **or** the `migrax` command-line tool |
| The startup library `migrax-micronaut` | Applying the pending migrations each time the application starts, before JPA | A dependency: see [Migrate at startup](#migrate-at-startup) |

**The tool for your terminal**, pick one:

=== "Maven plugin"

    ```xml title="pom.xml"
    <build>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.migrax</groupId>
          <artifactId>migrax</artifactId>
          <version>0.17.0</version>
        </plugin>
      </plugins>
    </build>
    ```

    Then run `mvn migrax:generate`, `mvn migrax:status` and so on in the project folder. See
    [Maven plugin](maven.md).

=== "Gradle plugin"

    ```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
    plugins {
        id("org.migrax") version "0.17.0"
    }
    ```

    Then run `./gradlew migraxGenerate`, `./gradlew migraxStatus` and so on. See
    [Gradle plugin](gradle.md).

=== "Command line tool"

    Install `migrax` once per machine ([Installation](../getting-started/installation.md)),
    then run `migrax generate`, `migrax status` and so on in the project folder. It works with
    any build, and nothing is added to the project.

**Only one of the two?**

- **Without the startup library** the application doesn't migrate by itself: run `migrate`
  yourself or in the deployment pipeline (`mvn migrax:migrate`, `./gradlew migraxMigrate`,
  `migrax migrate` or the [container image](../guides/containers-and-kubernetes.md)).
- **Without a tool for your terminal** there's no `generate`: write the migration files
  yourself, and the startup library still applies them.


## Command line

Migrax reads `application.yml` / `application.properties` and the environments in
`MICRONAUT_ENVIRONMENTS`:

```yaml
datasources:
  default:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/shop
    username: shop
    password: ${DB_PASSWORD}
jpa:
  default:
    properties:
      hibernate:
        hbm2ddl:
          auto: none
```

`DATASOURCES_DEFAULT_URL`, `DATASOURCES_DEFAULT_USERNAME` and `DATASOURCES_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` work
too. Without a `default` data source, Migrax uses the first one. Hibernate settings under
`jpa.default.properties.*` are passed to Hibernate.

!!! warning "Change the starter's `update`"

    Projects created from the Micronaut starter set `hbm2ddl.auto: update`. Set it to `none` or
    `validate`; `migrax doctor` shows the exact line.

## Naming

| Project uses | Naming | Example: `homepageURL` |
|---|---|---|
| Micronaut Data (`micronaut-data-hibernate-jpa`) | `micronaut` | `homepage_url` |
| Micronaut Hibernate JPA without Micronaut Data | `jpa` | `homepageURL` |

Micronaut Data converts names to snake_case with its own rule, which differs from other
snake_case rules for names like `myURL` (`my_url`) or `productSKU` (`product_sku`). It also
uses one shared `hibernate_sequence` for generated ids. Migrax matches both, and when Micronaut
Data is on the classpath it uses Micronaut's own naming class.

## Micronaut Data JDBC and R2DBC

New in Migrax 0.17.0.

With Micronaut Data JDBC or R2DBC (`@MappedEntity` entities instead of JPA's `@Entity`),
Migrax reads the mapping Micronaut's annotation processor compiled into your classes: tables,
columns, relations, join tables, embedded values and generated ids, named the way your
Micronaut Data version names them. Nothing to configure: build the project as usual (the
processor `micronaut-data-processor` must run), and `migrax doctor` shows
`Micronaut Data <version>`.

Micronaut 5 is compiled for Java 25, so run Migrax with Java 25 for a Micronaut 5 project
(`JAVA_HOME`); Migrax says so when the Java is too old.

Details and what isn't read: [Entity readers](../reference/hibernate.md#micronaut-data).

## Migrate at startup

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.migrax</groupId>
  <artifactId>migrax-micronaut</artifactId>
  <version>0.17.0</version>
</dependency>
```

Migrations run as soon as Micronaut creates the data source, **before** Hibernate starts, so
`hbm2ddl.auto: validate` checks the migrated schema.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `migrax.enabled` | `true` | Apply migrations at startup |
| `migrax.migrate-at-startup` | `true` | `false`: start without migrating, when a pipeline or a DBA runs the migrations; the health check and the pending gauge still report them ([details](../guides/observability.md#when-a-pipeline-migrates)) |
| `migrax.drift.check` | `off` | `warn` or `fail`: compare the database with the schema its migrations produce when the application starts; the build must put `.migrax/snapshot.json` into the application ([details](../guides/production-safety.md#drift-at-startup)) |
| `migrax.datasource` | `default` | Data source to migrate |
| `migrax.locations` | `db/migration` | Migration folders on the classpath, comma-separated |
| `migrax.java-package` | `db.migration` | Package of `JavaMigration` classes |
| `migrax.env` | | Environment: migrations marked `-- migrax:env <name>` run only there |
| `migrax.resume` | `false` | Re-run a failed migration marked `-- migrax:resume-safe` |
| `migrax.lock-timeout` | `0` | How long to wait while another instance migrates, for example `2m` when several start together |
| `migrax.placeholders.<name>` | | Values for `${name}` placeholders |
| `migrax.metrics.enabled` | `true` | Micrometer metrics of the migrations, when the application has a `MeterRegistry` ([Metrics and tracing](../guides/observability.md)) |
| `migrax.tracing.enabled` | `true` | OpenTelemetry spans of the migrations, when the application has an `OpenTelemetry` |
| `migrax.schemas` | | Schemas to migrate one after another |

## Health check

With `micronaut-management` in the application, Migrax adds a `migrax` health indicator: UP
when every migration is applied and none failed, was edited or is missing, DOWN otherwise, with
the counts as details (`/health`).

Source: https://migrax.org/frameworks/helidon/

# Helidon

## Helidon MP

### What you need

Migrax comes in two parts, and most projects use both:

| Part | What it's for | How you get it |
|---|---|---|
| A tool for your terminal | Writing migrations from your entities (`generate`) and looking after them: `status`, `lint`, `verify`, `rollback` and the other commands | The Maven plugin, the Gradle plugin **or** the `migrax` command-line tool |
| The startup library `migrax-helidon` | Applying the pending migrations each time the application starts, before JPA | A dependency: see [Migrate at startup](#migrate-at-startup) |

**The tool for your terminal**, pick one:

=== "Maven plugin"

    ```xml title="pom.xml"
    <build>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.migrax</groupId>
          <artifactId>migrax</artifactId>
          <version>0.17.0</version>
        </plugin>
      </plugins>
    </build>
    ```

    Then run `mvn migrax:generate`, `mvn migrax:status` and so on in the project folder. See
    [Maven plugin](maven.md).

=== "Gradle plugin"

    ```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
    plugins {
        id("org.migrax") version "0.17.0"
    }
    ```

    Then run `./gradlew migraxGenerate`, `./gradlew migraxStatus` and so on. See
    [Gradle plugin](gradle.md).

=== "Command line tool"

    Install `migrax` once per machine ([Installation](../getting-started/installation.md)),
    then run `migrax generate`, `migrax status` and so on in the project folder. It works with
    any build, and nothing is added to the project.

**Only one of the two?**

- **Without the startup library** the application doesn't migrate by itself: run `migrate`
  yourself or in the deployment pipeline (`mvn migrax:migrate`, `./gradlew migraxMigrate`,
  `migrax migrate` or the [container image](../guides/containers-and-kubernetes.md)).
- **Without a tool for your terminal** there's no `generate`: write the migration files
  yourself, and the startup library still applies them.


### Command line

Migrax reads `META-INF/microprofile-config.properties` (and the `mp.config.profile`) together
with `META-INF/persistence.xml`:

```properties title="META-INF/microprofile-config.properties"
javax.sql.DataSource.shop.dataSourceClassName=org.postgresql.ds.PGSimpleDataSource
javax.sql.DataSource.shop.dataSource.url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/shop
javax.sql.DataSource.shop.dataSource.user=shop
javax.sql.DataSource.shop.dataSource.password=secret
```

```xml title="META-INF/persistence.xml"
<persistence-unit name="shop" transaction-type="JTA">
  <jta-data-source>shop</jta-data-source>
  <properties>
    <property name="hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto" value="none"/>
  </properties>
</persistence-unit>
```

When several data sources are configured, Migrax uses the one `persistence.xml` names. The
`jdbcUrl`, `username` and `password` keys of other connection pools work too, and so do the
MicroProfile environment variables, such as `JAVAX_SQL_DATASOURCE_SHOP_DATASOURCE_URL`.
`hibernate.*` properties from `persistence.xml` are passed to Hibernate.

**Naming:** Helidon keeps Hibernate's default naming (`jpa`).

### Migrate at startup

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.migrax</groupId>
  <artifactId>migrax-helidon</artifactId>
  <version>0.17.0</version>
</dependency>
```

Migrations run when the application starts, before your own beans and before JPA is first used,
so `hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=validate` works. Settings go in `microprofile-config.properties`:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `migrax.enabled` | `true` | Apply migrations at startup |
| `migrax.migrate-at-startup` | `true` | `false`: start without migrating, when a pipeline or a DBA runs the migrations; the health check and the pending gauge still report them ([details](../guides/observability.md#when-a-pipeline-migrates)) |
| `migrax.drift.check` | `off` | `warn` or `fail`: compare the database with the schema its migrations produce when the application starts; the build must put `.migrax/snapshot.json` into the application ([details](../guides/production-safety.md#drift-at-startup)) |
| `migrax.datasource` | the one `persistence.xml` names, or the only one | Data source to migrate |
| `migrax.locations` | `db/migration` | Migration folders on the classpath, comma-separated |
| `migrax.java-package` | `db.migration` | Package of `JavaMigration` classes |
| `migrax.env` | | Environment: migrations marked `-- migrax:env <name>` run only there |
| `migrax.resume` | `false` | Re-run a failed migration marked `-- migrax:resume-safe` |
| `migrax.lock-timeout` | `0` | How long to wait while another instance migrates, for example `2m` when several start together |
| `migrax.placeholders.<name>` | | Values for `${name}` placeholders |
| `migrax.metrics.enabled` | `true` | Micrometer metrics of the migrations, when the application has a `MeterRegistry` ([Metrics and tracing](../guides/observability.md)) |
| `migrax.tracing.enabled` | `true` | OpenTelemetry spans of the migrations, when the application has an `OpenTelemetry` |
| `migrax.schemas` | | Schemas to migrate one after another |

### Readiness check

With `helidon-microprofile-health` in the application, Migrax adds a `migrax` readiness check:
UP when every migration is applied and none failed, was edited or is missing, DOWN otherwise,
with the counts as data (`/health/ready`).

## Helidon SE

Helidon SE uses its database client rather than JPA, so there are no entities to generate
migrations from. Write migrations with `migrax new` and apply them with `migrax migrate` in your
deployment ([SQL migrations for any language](../guides/sql-migrations-for-any-language.md) explains
this setup). Migrax reads the connection from `application.yaml`:

```yaml
db:
  connection:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/shop
    username: shop
    password: secret
```

Source: https://migrax.org/frameworks/jakarta-ee/

# Jakarta EE and plain Hibernate

Any project with JPA entities works, with or without an application framework.

## What you need

Migrax comes in two parts, and most projects use both:

| Part | What it's for | How you get it |
|---|---|---|
| A tool for your terminal | Writing migrations from your entities (`generate`) and looking after them: `status`, `lint`, `verify`, `rollback` and the other commands | The Maven plugin, the Gradle plugin **or** the `migrax` command-line tool |
| The startup library `migrax-jakarta-ee` | Applying the pending migrations each time the application is deployed, before JPA | A dependency: see [Migrate at startup](#migrate-at-startup) |

**The tool for your terminal**, pick one:

=== "Maven plugin"

    ```xml title="pom.xml"
    <build>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.migrax</groupId>
          <artifactId>migrax</artifactId>
          <version>0.17.0</version>
        </plugin>
      </plugins>
    </build>
    ```

    Then run `mvn migrax:generate`, `mvn migrax:status` and so on in the project folder. See
    [Maven plugin](maven.md).

=== "Gradle plugin"

    ```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
    plugins {
        id("org.migrax") version "0.17.0"
    }
    ```

    Then run `./gradlew migraxGenerate`, `./gradlew migraxStatus` and so on. See
    [Gradle plugin](gradle.md).

=== "Command line tool"

    Install `migrax` once per machine ([Installation](../getting-started/installation.md)),
    then run `migrax generate`, `migrax status` and so on in the project folder. It works with
    any build, and nothing is added to the project.

**Only one of the two?**

- **Without the startup library** the application doesn't migrate by itself: run `migrate`
  yourself or in the deployment pipeline (`mvn migrax:migrate`, `./gradlew migraxMigrate`,
  `migrax migrate` or the [container image](../guides/containers-and-kubernetes.md)).
- **Without a tool for your terminal** there's no `generate`: write the migration files
  yourself, and the startup library still applies them.


## Database settings

Migrax reads the first persistence unit in `src/main/resources/META-INF/persistence.xml`:

```xml
<persistence-unit name="shop">
  <properties>
    <property name="jakarta.persistence.jdbc.url" value="jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/shop"/>
    <property name="jakarta.persistence.jdbc.user" value="shop"/>
    <property name="jakarta.persistence.jdbc.password" value="secret"/>
    <property name="hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto" value="none"/>
  </properties>
</persistence-unit>
```

`javax.persistence.jdbc.*` and `hibernate.connection.*` work too. On an application server, the
data source is usually defined in the server's own configuration, which the `migrax` command
can't read: give it the connection with environment variables or options, or let the
[startup integration](#migrate-at-startup) migrate inside the server.

```bash
export MIGRAX_DATABASE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/shop
export MIGRAX_DATABASE_USER=shop
export MIGRAX_DATABASE_PASSWORD=secret
migrax migrate
```

## Naming

Plain Hibernate keeps names as written (`jpa` naming). A physical or implicit naming strategy in
`persistence.xml` (`hibernate.physical_naming_strategy`) is used when Migrax reads the mapping.

## Running migrations

Run `migrax migrate` as a step of your deployment, before the new version starts, or let the
application migrate when it starts on the server.

## Migrate at startup

Add the integration to your WAR or EAR:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.migrax</groupId>
  <artifactId>migrax-jakarta-ee</artifactId>
  <version>0.17.0</version>
</dependency>
```

When the application starts, Migrax applies the migrations from `db/migration` to the data
source your `persistence.xml` names, as the server provides it. You don't repeat the
connection settings. It is tested on WildFly and Payara and uses only standard Jakarta EE (CDI
and JNDI), so it works on other servers too.

```xml
<persistence-unit name="shop">
  <jta-data-source>java:app/jdbc/shop</jta-data-source>
  <properties>
    <property name="jakarta.persistence.schema-generation.database.action" value="none"/>
  </properties>
</persistence-unit>
```

Keep the schema generation at `none`. The server starts JPA while it deploys the application,
before any application code runs, so Hibernate's `validate` would check the schema before the
migrations. Validate in CI with `migrax verify` instead.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `migrax.enabled` | `true` | Apply migrations at startup |
| `migrax.migrate-at-startup` | `true` | `false`: start without migrating, when a pipeline or a DBA runs the migrations; the health check and the pending gauge still report them ([details](../guides/observability.md#when-a-pipeline-migrates)) |
| `migrax.drift.check` | `off` | `warn` or `fail`: compare the database with the schema its migrations produce when the application starts; the build must put `.migrax/snapshot.json` into the application ([details](../guides/production-safety.md#drift-at-startup)) |
| `migrax.datasource` | the data source `persistence.xml` names | JNDI name of the data source to migrate |
| `migrax.locations` | `db/migration` | Migration folders on the classpath, comma-separated |
| `migrax.java-package` | `db.migration` | Package of `JavaMigration` classes |
| `migrax.env` | | Environment: migrations marked `-- migrax:env <name>` run only there |
| `migrax.resume` | `false` | Re-run a failed migration marked `-- migrax:resume-safe` |
| `migrax.lock-timeout` | `0` | How long to wait while another instance migrates, for example `2m` |
| `migrax.placeholders.<name>` | | Values for `${name}` placeholders |
| `migrax.metrics.enabled` | `true` | Micrometer metrics of the migrations, when the application has a `MeterRegistry` ([Metrics and tracing](../guides/observability.md)) |
| `migrax.tracing.enabled` | `true` | OpenTelemetry spans of the migrations, when the application has an `OpenTelemetry` |
| `migrax.schemas` | | Schemas to migrate one after another |

Jakarta EE has no standard place for application settings, so Migrax reads them from
`migrax.properties` in the application (`src/main/resources`), from MicroProfile Config where
the server has it, from environment variables (`MIGRAX_DATASOURCE`, `MIGRAX_LOCATIONS`,
`MIGRAX_PLACEHOLDERS_<NAME>`, ...) and from system properties. Each one overrides the one
before.

!!! note "JPA providers"

    Migrax reads the mapping through the server's JPA provider: Hibernate (WildFly), EclipseLink
    (Payara, GlassFish) or OpenJPA (TomEE). With another JPA provider it scans the annotations
    and applies Hibernate's naming rules; check the generated names, and use
    `migrax drift --entities` to compare.


---

Source: https://migrax.org/frameworks/any-language/

# Any language

Migrax isn't only for Java. Any application that keeps its database changes as SQL files can
use it to apply them: Python, Node.js, Go, .NET, PHP, Ruby or anything else. You write the
migrations; Migrax runs them once and in order, records them, and refuses to run a file that
changed after it was applied. You don't need a second migration tool next to your framework.

| What you get | |
|---|---|
| Numbered migrations, applied once and in order | `0001_create_customer.sql`, `0002_add_email.sql` |
| Repeatable migrations for views and functions | `R__customer_view.sql`, run again when they change |
| A history table, checksums and a lock | Safe with several instances starting at the same time |
| Rollback scripts | `rollback/0002_add_email.sql`, run by `migrax rollback` |
| Checks before anything runs | `migrax lint` finds statements that lock tables or lose data |
| A status overview | `migrax status`, also as JSON for scripts |

The commands that compare the database with Java entities (`generate`, `check`, `drift` and
`verify`) have nothing to read in such a project; everything else works the same.

## Two ways to run it

| | Needs | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| [Container image](../guides/containers-and-kubernetes.md) | Docker | Docker Compose, Kubernetes, CI. Drivers for PostgreSQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite and H2 included |
| [Command line](../getting-started/installation.md) | Java 17 or newer | Running it on your machine like any other development tool |

## In three steps

1. Put your SQL files in a folder, for example `db/migrations`:

    ```sql title="db/migrations/0001_create_customer.sql"
    CREATE TABLE customer (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL);
    ```

2. Tell Migrax the database, as a JDBC URL:

    ```bash
    export MIGRAX_DATABASE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/shop
    export MIGRAX_DATABASE_USER=shop
    export MIGRAX_DATABASE_PASSWORD=secret
    export MIGRAX_LOCATIONS=filesystem:db/migrations
    ```

3. Apply the migrations:

    === "Container image"

        ```bash
        docker run --rm --network host \
          -v "$PWD/db/migrations:/migrations:ro" \
          -e MIGRAX_DATABASE_URL \
          -e MIGRAX_DATABASE_USER \
          -e MIGRAX_DATABASE_PASSWORD \
          ghcr.io/fsmutimeer/migrax:0.17.0 migrate
        ```

        The image reads the migrations from `/migrations`, so `MIGRAX_LOCATIONS` isn't needed
        there.

    === "Command line"

        ```console
        $ migrax migrate
        Applying migration '0001_create_customer.sql'...
        Successfully applied migration '0001_create_customer.sql'.
        Applied 1 migration(s); 1 total in db/migrations.
        ```

        The command line also needs the database's JDBC driver: see
        [Drivers](../guides/sql-migrations-for-any-language.md#drivers).

## Before your application starts

With Docker Compose, run Migrax as a service of its own and start the application only after it
finished:

```yaml title="compose.yaml"
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:17
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: shop
      POSTGRES_USER: shop
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U shop -d shop"]
      interval: 2s
      retries: 30

  migrate:
    image: ghcr.io/fsmutimeer/migrax:0.17.0
    command: migrate --lock-timeout 2m
    volumes:
      - ./db/migrations:/migrations:ro
    environment:
      MIGRAX_DATABASE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/shop
      MIGRAX_DATABASE_USER: shop
      MIGRAX_DATABASE_PASSWORD: secret
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy

  app:
    build: .
    depends_on:
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
```

When a migration fails, `migrate` exits with code 1 and the application doesn't start. In
Kubernetes, the same image runs as an init container or a Job: see
[Containers and Kubernetes](../guides/containers-and-kubernetes.md).

## From your project's scripts

Call Migrax from the task runner your project already has, so everyone runs the same command:

=== "Node.js"

    ```json title="package.json"
    {
      "scripts": {
        "db:migrate": "migrax migrate",
        "db:status": "migrax status",
        "db:new": "migrax new"
      }
    }
    ```

    `npm run db:new -- add_email` creates the next numbered file.

=== "PHP"

    ```json title="composer.json"
    {
      "scripts": {
        "db:migrate": "migrax migrate",
        "db:status": "migrax status"
      }
    }
    ```

=== "Python, Go, Ruby, .NET"

    ```makefile title="Makefile"
    db-migrate:
    	migrax migrate

    db-status:
    	migrax status
    ```

Settings in environment variables (or a `.env` file your shell loads) keep these scripts free of
passwords. Every setting is listed in [Configuration](../reference/configuration.md).

## In CI

Check the migrations on every pull request, before they reach a database:

```bash
migrax lint --strict
migrax migrate --dry-run
```

`lint` needs no database; `migrate --dry-run` connects and shows what would run. More in
[Continuous integration](../guides/ci.md).

## Next

- [SQL migrations for any language](../guides/sql-migrations-for-any-language.md): drivers, writing
  migrations, a database that already has tables, rollbacks and `migrax doctor`, step by step.
- [Moving existing migrations to Migrax](../guides/switching-tools.md), when your project
  already has a history of applied migrations.
- [Advanced migrations](../guides/advanced-migrations.md): placeholders, callbacks, environments
  and preconditions.

Source: https://migrax.org/frameworks/maven/

# Maven plugin

Everything the command line does is also available as Maven goals, which is handy in CI or when
you prefer not to install the CLI.

## Setup

```xml title="pom.xml"
<build>
  <plugins>
    <plugin>
      <groupId>org.migrax</groupId>
      <artifactId>migrax</artifactId>
      <version>0.17.0</version>
    </plugin>
  </plugins>
</build>
```

Maven downloads it from Maven Central. Goals compile the project and use its runtime classpath,
so no other configuration is needed.

## Goals

```bash
mvn migrax:generate
mvn migrax:migrate
mvn migrax:status
```

| Goal | Same as |
|---|---|
| `migrax:generate` | `migrax generate` |
| `migrax:migrate` | `migrax migrate` |
| `migrax:status` | `migrax status` |
| `migrax:plan` | `migrax plan` |
| `migrax:check` | `migrax check` |
| `migrax:lint` | `migrax lint` |
| `migrax:verify` | `migrax verify` |
| `migrax:drift` | `migrax drift` |
| `migrax:diff` | `migrax diff` (`-Dmigrax.source=<url>`) |
| `migrax:report` | `migrax report` |
| `migrax:rollback` | `migrax rollback` |
| `migrax:repair` | `migrax repair` |
| `migrax:baseline` | `migrax baseline` (`-Dmigrax.version=<migration>`) |
| `migrax:clean` | `migrax clean` |
| `migrax:backups` | `migrax backups` (`-Dmigrax.drop=true`, `-Dmigrax.migration=<number>`) |
| `migrax:new` | `migrax new` |
| `migrax:squash` | `migrax squash` |
| `migrax:merge` | `migrax merge` |
| `migrax:import` | `migrax import` (`-Dmigrax.from=flyway` or `liquibase`) |
| `migrax:package-snapshot` | No command: copies `.migrax/snapshot.json` into the application for [drift at startup](../guides/production-safety.md#drift-at-startup) |

## Options

Options are `-Dmigrax.*` properties (or `<configuration>` elements of the same name):

| Property | CLI option | Goals |
|---|---|---|
| `migrax.allowDestructive=true` | `--allow-destructive` | generate |
| `migrax.keepData=true` | `--keep-data` | generate |
| `migrax.renames=customers.email=contact_email` | `--rename` | generate |
| `migrax.renameTables=client=customer` | `--rename-table` | generate |
| `migrax.name=split_name` | `--name` | generate, new |
| `migrax.safe=true` | `--safe` | generate |
| `migrax.zeroDowntime=true` | `--zero-downtime` | generate |
| `migrax.contract=true` | `--contract` | generate |
| `migrax.dryRun=true` | `--dry-run` | migrate, rollback, clean, baseline |
| `migrax.resume=true` | `--resume` | migrate |
| `migrax.sql=true` | `--sql` | migrate |
| `migrax.lockTimeout=2m` | `--lock-timeout` | migrate, rollback, repair, clean, generate |
| `migrax.steps=2`, `migrax.to=<migration>` | `--steps`, `--to` | rollback (`to` also migrate) |
| `migrax.confirm=true` | `--yes` | rollback, repair, clean, baseline, backups |
| `migrax.action=applied` | `--action` | repair |
| `migrax.impact=true` | `--impact` | plan |
| `migrax.all=true`, `migrax.strict=true` | `--all`, `--strict` | lint |
| `migrax.verifyUrl=<jdbc-url>`, `migrax.skipRollbacks=true` | `--url`, `--skip-rollbacks` | verify |
| `migrax.entities=true` | `--entities` | drift |
| `migrax.html=target/migrax-report.html` | `--html` | report |
| `migrax.java=true` | `--java` | new |
| `migrax.url`, `migrax.user`, `migrax.password` | `--url`, `--user`, `--password` | all |
| `migrax.database=billing` | `--database` | all |
| `migrax.package`, `migrax.naming`, `migrax.dialect`, `migrax.locations`, `migrax.schemas` | same names | all |

Hints in the output use Maven syntax, for example:

```console
$ mvn migrax:generate
[ERROR] Review them, then run 'mvn migrax:generate -Dmigrax.allowDestructive=true'.
```

Source: https://migrax.org/frameworks/gradle/

# Gradle plugin

## Setup

```kotlin title="settings.gradle.kts"
pluginManagement {
    repositories {
        mavenCentral()
        gradlePluginPortal()
    }
}
```

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
plugins {
    java
    id("org.migrax") version "0.17.0"
}

repositories {
    mavenCentral()          // the plugin loads the Migrax library from here
}

migrax {
    packageName.set("com.example.shop")   // optional; defaults to the project group
}
```

The plugin also adds `.migrax/snapshot.json` to the application's resources as
`META-INF/migrax/snapshot.json`, so the application can check for
[drift at startup](../guides/production-safety.md#drift-at-startup).

## Tasks

| Task | Same as |
|---|---|
| `migraxGenerate` | `migrax generate` |
| `migraxMigrate` | `migrax migrate` |
| `migraxStatus` | `migrax status` |
| `migraxPlan` | `migrax plan` |
| `migraxCheck` | `migrax check` |
| `migraxLint` | `migrax lint` |
| `migraxVerify` | `migrax verify` |
| `migraxDrift` | `migrax drift` |
| `migraxRollback` | `migrax rollback` |
| `migraxRepair` | `migrax repair` |
| `migraxNew` | `migrax new` |
| `migraxSquash` | `migrax squash` |
| `migraxMerge` | `migrax merge` |

Pass CLI options with `-Pmigrax.args`:

```bash
gradle migraxGenerate -Pmigrax.args="--allow-destructive"
gradle migraxRollback -Pmigrax.args="--steps 2 --yes"
```

## The `migrax` extension

| Property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `packageName` | Entity package |
| `url`, `user`, `password` | Database connection (default: application config) |
| `locations` | Migration folders, comma-separated, e.g. `classpath:db/migration` |
| `naming` | `spring`, `jpa`, `jpa-snake` or `micronaut` |
| `dialect` | `postgresql`, `mysql`, `mariadb`, `sqlserver`, `oracle` or `h2` |
| `args` | Extra arguments for every task, e.g. `--verbose` |
| `version` | Migrax version used to run the tasks |


---

Source: https://migrax.org/reference/cli/

# CLI commands

Run `migrax help <command>` for the same information in the terminal. Run every command from the
service folder (the one with `pom.xml` or `build.gradle`), or pass `--dir <path>`.

## Options for every command

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use the classes and dependencies from the last build |
| `--refresh` | Re-resolve dependencies even if cached |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output (`plan`, `status`, `check`, `lint`, `drift`, `diff`, `verify`) |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | Show debug output, Hibernate's own log and stack traces |
| `--no-input` | Never ask questions (the default when input is not a terminal) |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Error, failed check, or failed migration |
| `2` | Differences found: `check` (entity changes without a migration), `drift` (database differs), `diff` (the two databases differ) |

## Getting started

### init

```
migrax init
```

Creates the .migrax folder and the migration folder, then shows the entity package, database, dialect and naming Migrax detected. Safe to run more than once.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--package <name>` | Entity package (default: MIGRAX_PACKAGE or pom groupId) |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--naming <strategy>` | spring, jpa, jpa-snake or micronaut (default: detected) |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### doctor

```
migrax doctor
```

Runs every check Migrax needs and explains how to fix anything that fails. Exits with code 1 when a check fails.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--env <name>` | Environment for migrations marked '-- migrax:env' |
| `--package <name>` | Entity package (default: MIGRAX_PACKAGE or pom groupId) |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--extractor <mode>` | auto, hibernate, eclipselink, openjpa, spring-data-jdbc, micronaut-data or annotations (default: auto) |
| `--schema-file <path>` | SQL file with the desired schema, instead of entities |
| `--scratch-url <url>` | Empty database to read the schema file in (default: Docker) |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### mcp

```
migrax mcp [--allow-generate]
```

Runs a Model Context Protocol server on stdin/stdout, so AI assistants such as Claude Code can
call status, check, plan, lint, drift, doctor, verify and show_migration as tools and read their
JSON results. It never changes a database: migrate, rollback, repair and clean are not offered.
`--allow-generate` also offers generate, which writes migration files for the person to review.
Claude Code: `claude mcp add migrax -- migrax mcp`. See
[Using Migrax with AI assistants](../guides/ai-assistants.md).

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--allow-generate` | Also offer the generate tool (writes migration files) |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### import

```
migrax import flyway|liquibase
```

flyway: records every migration in flyway_schema_history as applied, so Migrax continues where
Flyway stopped; `V*__` and `R__` files keep working. liquibase: writes a baseline migration with
the current schema and records it. Afterwards run `migrax generate` to start managing changes,
and remove Flyway or Liquibase from the project. See
[Switching from Flyway or Liquibase](../guides/switching-tools.md).

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--table <name>` | Flyway history table (default: flyway_schema_history) |
| `--name <name>` | Migration file name (default: next number + description) |
| `--schema <name>` | Database schema to read |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--dialect <name>` | postgresql, cockroachdb, yugabytedb, mysql, mariadb, tidb, sqlserver, oracle, h2, hsqldb, derby, sqlite |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

## Everyday

### baseline

```
migrax baseline <migration> [--dry-run] --yes
```

For a database whose tables already exist (created by hand, by a script or by another tool): records every versioned migration up to and including `<migration>` as applied without running it. `migrax migrate` then runs only the later ones. Refused when the database already has migration history. `--yes` confirms the change to migration history.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Show what would happen without doing it |
| `--yes, -y` | Confirm without asking |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--env <name>` | Environment for migrations marked '-- migrax:env' |
| `--schemas <a,b>` | Run for each schema (multi-tenant) |
| `--lock-timeout <time>` | Wait this long while another process migrates (e.g. 2m) |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--java-package <pkg>` | Package of Java migrations (default: db.migration) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### generate

*Alias:* `makemigrations`

```
migrax generate [--name <name>] [--allow-destructive [--keep-data]] [--safe]
migrax generate --zero-downtime [--name <name>] [--allow-destructive]
migrax generate --contract
```

Compiles the project if needed, compares the entities with `.migrax/snapshot.json` and writes a numbered SQL file plus a rollback script (`rollback/<file>`). On the first run, with no snapshot, the current database schema is the baseline: its tables are written to `0001_baseline.sql`, which that database records as applied without running it. When a column or table seems renamed, Migrax asks (or pass `--rename` / `--rename-table`) so the data is kept. Drops need `--allow-destructive`; with `--keep-data`, dropped tables and columns go to `migrax_backup_*` tables and the rollback script restores them (`migrax backups` lists and drops those tables). `--safe` (PostgreSQL, CockroachDB) builds indexes and constraints on existing tables without blocking writes, in a second migration. `--zero-downtime` splits the change so the old and new application versions can run at the same time: an expand migration now (new columns and tables, a renamed column kept equal to its old name by a trigger, a renamed table's old name as a view) and a contract migration for the next release (drops, NOT NULL, narrower types, new constraints). The contract migration waits in `.migrax/pending/`; `generate --contract` adds it to the migration folder. Always review the generated SQL; Migrax lints it for you.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--name <name>` | Migration file name (default: next number + description) |
| `--allow-destructive` | Allow drops and narrowing type changes |
| `--keep-data` | Keep dropped data in backup tables the rollback restores |
| `--safe` | Non-blocking indexes and constraints (PostgreSQL, CockroachDB) |
| `--zero-downtime` | Split into an expand migration now and a contract one later |
| `--contract` | Add the waiting contract migrations to the migration folder |
| `--rename t.old=new` | Treat a column change as a rename (comma-separated) |
| `--rename-table old=new` | Treat a table change as a rename |
| `--no-input` | Never ask questions |
| `--lock-timeout <time>` | Wait this long while another process migrates (e.g. 2m) |
| `--dialect <name>` | postgresql, cockroachdb, yugabytedb, mysql, mariadb, tidb, sqlserver, oracle, h2, hsqldb, derby, sqlite |
| `--package <name>` | Entity package (default: MIGRAX_PACKAGE or pom groupId) |
| `--naming <strategy>` | spring, jpa, jpa-snake or micronaut (default: detected) |
| `--extractor <mode>` | auto, hibernate, eclipselink, openjpa, spring-data-jdbc, micronaut-data or annotations (default: auto) |
| `--schema-file <path>` | SQL file with the desired schema, instead of entities |
| `--scratch-url <url>` | Empty database to read the schema file in (default: Docker) |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--schema <name>` | Database schema to read |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--refresh` | Re-resolve dependencies even if cached |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### migrate

```
migrax migrate [--to <migration>] [--sql | --dry-run] [--resume] [--schemas a,b]
```

Applies pending SQL and Java migrations in order, then new or changed repeatable `R__*.sql` migrations, with beforeMigrate/afterMigrate callbacks and `${placeholders}`. `--to` applies versioned migrations only up to and including the given one; repeatable migrations then wait for the next migrate without `--to`. `--sql` prints the SQL script of what migrate would do, for a DBA to review and run with the database's own tool; nothing changes. `--dry-run` lists and lints pending migrations without changing the database. `--schemas` runs the migrations once per schema (multi-tenant). `--resume` re-runs a failed migration only if it is marked `-- migrax:resume-safe`.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--to <migration>` | Last migration to apply, keep or squash up to |
| `--env <name>` | Environment for migrations marked '-- migrax:env' |
| `--sql` | Print the SQL script without running it (for a DBA) |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would happen without doing it |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--resume` | Re-run a failed resume-safe migration |
| `--lock-timeout <time>` | Wait this long while another process migrates (e.g. 2m) |
| `--schemas <a,b>` | Run for each schema (multi-tenant) |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--java-package <pkg>` | Package of Java migrations (default: db.migration) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### status

*Alias:* `showmigrations`

```
migrax status [--json]
```

Lists migrations as applied [X], pending [ ] or a problem [!], without changing the database. Exits with code 1 when a migration failed, changed or is missing.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--env <name>` | Environment for migrations marked '-- migrax:env' |
| `--schemas <a,b>` | Run for each schema (multi-tenant) |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--java-package <pkg>` | Package of Java migrations (default: db.migration) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### plan

*Alias:* `sqlmigrate`

```
migrax plan [--impact] [--json]
```

Shows the operations and SQL for current entity changes without writing files. `--impact` adds the estimated size of each affected table from the database.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--impact` | Show affected table sizes (needs the database) |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--dialect <name>` | postgresql, cockroachdb, yugabytedb, mysql, mariadb, tidb, sqlserver, oracle, h2, hsqldb, derby, sqlite |
| `--rename t.old=new` | Treat a column change as a rename (comma-separated) |
| `--rename-table old=new` | Treat a table change as a rename |
| `--package <name>` | Entity package (default: MIGRAX_PACKAGE or pom groupId) |
| `--naming <strategy>` | spring, jpa, jpa-snake or micronaut (default: detected) |
| `--extractor <mode>` | auto, hibernate, eclipselink, openjpa, spring-data-jdbc, micronaut-data or annotations (default: auto) |
| `--schema-file <path>` | SQL file with the desired schema, instead of entities |
| `--scratch-url <url>` | Empty database to read the schema file in (default: Docker) |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--refresh` | Re-resolve dependencies even if cached |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### rollback

```
migrax rollback [--steps n | --to <migration>] [--dry-run] --yes
```

Runs the rollback script of the newest applied migration (or several) and removes it from the history. generate writes rollback scripts to `rollback/<file>`; Java migrations roll back with `JavaMigration.rollback`. Restores structure, not deleted data.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--steps <n>` | Number of migrations to roll back |
| `--to <migration>` | Last migration to apply, keep or squash up to |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would happen without doing it |
| `--yes, -y` | Confirm without asking |
| `--schemas <a,b>` | Run for each schema (multi-tenant) |
| `--lock-timeout <time>` | Wait this long while another process migrates (e.g. 2m) |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### new

```
migrax new <name> [--java]
```

Creates the next numbered SQL file for hand-written changes such as data migrations, with an empty rollback script. `--java` creates a JavaMigration class instead.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--java` | Create a Java migration |

## Safety and CI

### check

```
migrax check [--json]
```

Exits with code 2 when the entities differ from `.migrax/snapshot.json`, and with 1 when two migrations share a number (run `migrax merge`).

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--package <name>` | Entity package (default: MIGRAX_PACKAGE or pom groupId) |
| `--naming <strategy>` | spring, jpa, jpa-snake or micronaut (default: detected) |
| `--extractor <mode>` | auto, hibernate, eclipselink, openjpa, spring-data-jdbc, micronaut-data or annotations (default: auto) |
| `--schema-file <path>` | SQL file with the desired schema, instead of entities |
| `--scratch-url <url>` | Empty database to read the schema file in (default: Docker) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--refresh` | Re-resolve dependencies even if cached |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### lint

```
migrax lint [files...] [--all] [--strict] [--json]
```

Checks pending migrations (or the given files, or `--all`) for statements that block tables, fail on existing data, or break running application instances, and suggests safe alternatives. Exits with 1 on errors, or on warnings with `--strict`. Silence a finding with `-- migrax:lint-ignore MX001` before the statement.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--all` | Lint every migration, not only pending ones |
| `--strict` | Fail on warnings too |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--dialect <name>` | postgresql, cockroachdb, yugabytedb, mysql, mariadb, tidb, sqlserver, oracle, h2, hsqldb, derby, sqlite |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### verify

```
migrax verify [--url <scratch-db>] [--skip-rollbacks]
```

Starts a throwaway database (H2, HSQLDB and Derby in memory, Docker for other engines), applies every migration, then checks the result: Hibernate's schema validation when Hibernate is in the project, otherwise a structural comparison with the entities. It also tests every rollback script on its own: it rolls the migration back, applies it again and checks that the schema is the same, so a broken script is named.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--image <image>` | Docker image for the throwaway database |
| `--skip-rollbacks` | Do not test rollback scripts |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--env <name>` | Environment for migrations marked '-- migrax:env' |
| `--dialect <name>` | postgresql, cockroachdb, yugabytedb, mysql, mariadb, tidb, sqlserver, oracle, h2, hsqldb, derby, sqlite |
| `--package <name>` | Entity package (default: MIGRAX_PACKAGE or pom groupId) |
| `--naming <strategy>` | spring, jpa, jpa-snake or micronaut (default: detected) |
| `--extractor <mode>` | auto, hibernate, eclipselink, openjpa, spring-data-jdbc, micronaut-data or annotations (default: auto) |
| `--schema-file <path>` | SQL file with the desired schema, instead of entities |
| `--scratch-url <url>` | Empty database to read the schema file in (default: Docker) |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### drift

```
migrax drift [--entities] [--json]
```

Reads the database schema and reports manual changes: missing or extra tables, columns, keys and unique constraints, nullability and type differences. Compares with the snapshot (what migrations produce) or, with `--entities`, the entities. Exits with code 2 when drift is found.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--entities` | Compare with the entities instead of the snapshot |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--env <name>` | Environment for migrations marked '-- migrax:env' |
| `--schema <name>` | Database schema to read |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--package <name>` | Entity package (default: MIGRAX_PACKAGE or pom groupId) |
| `--naming <strategy>` | spring, jpa, jpa-snake or micronaut (default: detected) |
| `--extractor <mode>` | auto, hibernate, eclipselink, openjpa, spring-data-jdbc, micronaut-data or annotations (default: auto) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### diff

```
migrax diff <source-url> [--sql] [--json]
```

Compares the schema of the source database (for example staging) with the project's database (for example production; set it with `--url`) and lists the changes that would make the project's database match: tables, columns, types, keys, indexes, checks and comments. `--sql` prints them as one SQL script to review. Both must be the same kind of database. Exits with code 2 when they differ. The source's user and password come from `--source-user` and `--source-password-file`, `MIGRAX_SOURCE_USER` and `MIGRAX_SOURCE_PASSWORD`, or the URL itself.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--sql` | Print the SQL script without running it (for a DBA) |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--source-user <name>` | User of the source database |
| `--source-password-file <path>` | Read the source database's password from a file |
| `--schema <name>` | Database schema to read |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### environments

```
migrax environments [--environments <a,b>] [--no-drift] [--timeout <duration>] [--json]
```

Asks each environment's database (`migrax.environments.<name>.url`) which migrations it has applied, lists what is pending there and whether its schema drifted from the snapshot, without changing anything. Migrations marked `-- migrax:env` count only in the environments they name. Exits with code 1 when an environment can't be reached or a migration failed, changed or is missing there, and 2 when drift is found; pending migrations alone exit with 0.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--environments <a,b>` | Environments to show, in this order (default: all configured) |
| `--no-drift` | Don't compare the schemas with the snapshot |
| `--timeout <duration>` | How long to wait for each database (default: 30s) |
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--java-package <pkg>` | Package of Java migrations (default: db.migration) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### report

```
migrax report [--html <file>]
```

Writes one HTML page (default `migrax-report.html`) for reviews and CI artifacts: the schema with a diagram, entity changes that have no migration yet, every migration with its status and lint findings, and drift between the database and the snapshot. Parts that need the database are skipped when it can't be reached.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--html <file>` | Where to write the page (default: migrax-report.html) |
| `--env <name>` | Environment for migrations marked '-- migrax:env' |
| `--schemas <a,b>` | Run for each schema (multi-tenant) |
| `--dialect <name>` | postgresql, cockroachdb, yugabytedb, mysql, mariadb, tidb, sqlserver, oracle, h2, hsqldb, derby, sqlite |
| `--package <name>` | Entity package (default: MIGRAX_PACKAGE or pom groupId) |
| `--naming <strategy>` | spring, jpa, jpa-snake or micronaut (default: detected) |
| `--extractor <mode>` | auto, hibernate, eclipselink, openjpa, spring-data-jdbc, micronaut-data or annotations (default: auto) |
| `--schema-file <path>` | SQL file with the desired schema, instead of entities |
| `--scratch-url <url>` | Empty database to read the schema file in (default: Docker) |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

## Maintenance

### squash

*Alias:* `squashmigrations`

```
migrax squash --to <migration> [--optimize]
```

Writes one migration that replaces all migrations up to `--to`. Databases that already applied them record it without running it; new databases run just the squashed file. `--optimize` writes only the resulting schema (data statements are dropped). Delete the old files once every environment has run migrate.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--to <migration>` | Last migration to apply, keep or squash up to |
| `--name <name>` | Migration file name (default: next number + description) |
| `--optimize` | Squash to the resulting schema only |
| `--dialect <name>` | postgresql, cockroachdb, yugabytedb, mysql, mariadb, tidb, sqlserver, oracle, h2, hsqldb, derby, sqlite |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### merge

```
migrax merge
```

Renumbers migrations that share a number after a git merge (the one added later moves to the next free number) and rebuilds a snapshot that has merge conflicts.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--dialect <name>` | postgresql, cockroachdb, yugabytedb, mysql, mariadb, tidb, sqlserver, oracle, h2, hsqldb, derby, sqlite |
| `--package <name>` | Entity package (default: MIGRAX_PACKAGE or pom groupId) |
| `--naming <strategy>` | spring, jpa, jpa-snake or micronaut (default: detected) |
| `--extractor <mode>` | auto, hibernate, eclipselink, openjpa, spring-data-jdbc, micronaut-data or annotations (default: auto) |
| `--schema-file <path>` | SQL file with the desired schema, instead of entities |
| `--scratch-url <url>` | Empty database to read the schema file in (default: Docker) |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### repair

```
migrax repair <migration>... --action applied|retry|forget --yes
```

Use only after inspecting the database.

- `--action applied`: every statement took effect, so record the migration as applied.
- `--action retry`: you restored the database, so clear the failure and let it run again.
- `--action forget`: you deleted applied migration files on purpose, so remove them from the
  history. The database keeps the changes they made. Accepts several migrations at once.

`--yes` confirms the change to the migration history.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--action <action>` | applied, retry or forget |
| `--yes, -y` | Confirm without asking |
| `--lock-timeout <time>` | Wait this long while another process migrates (e.g. 2m) |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--locations <paths>` | Migration folders, comma-separated (e.g. filesystem:db/sql) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### clean

```
migrax clean [--dry-run] [--yes]
```

Empties the database so `migrax migrate` can rebuild it from the migrations: drops every table
(the migration history too), view and sequence in the configured schema. Data is deleted and
can't be restored. Migration files and the snapshot are not touched. Asks before dropping;
`--yes` confirms without asking. `--dry-run` lists what would be dropped. Set
`MIGRAX_CLEAN_DISABLED=true` on servers where clean must never run.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would happen without doing it |
| `--yes, -y` | Confirm without asking |
| `--lock-timeout <time>` | Wait this long while another process migrates (e.g. 2m) |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--schema <name>` | Database schema to read |
| `--schemas <a,b>` | Run for each schema (multi-tenant) |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### backups

```
migrax backups [--drop [<migration>] --yes]
```

Lists the `migrax_backup_*` tables that migrations generated with `--keep-data` keep dropped
data in; their rollback scripts restore it from there. Once you are sure you won't roll a
migration back, drop its backups: `--drop` removes them all, or only those of one migration
(`--drop 0005`). Asks before dropping; `--yes` confirms without asking.

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable output |
| `--drop [<migration>]` | Drop the backup tables (all, or one migration's) |
| `--yes, -y` | Confirm without asking |
| `--url <jdbc-url>` | Database URL (default: application config) |
| `--user <name>` | Database user |
| `--password <secret>` | Database password (prefer env vars) |
| `--password-file <path>` | Read the database password from a file (mounted secret) |
| `--schema <name>` | Database schema to read |
| `--classpath <paths>` | Extra classpath; skips Maven/Gradle resolution |
| `--no-build` | Do not run Maven/Gradle; use compiled classes |
| `--database <name>` | Work on `migrax.databases.<name>` instead of the default database |
| `--dir <path>` | Project folder (default: current folder) |

### help

```
migrax help [command]
```

Shows general help, or help for one command.


---

Source: https://migrax.org/reference/configuration/

# Configuration

Most projects need no configuration: Migrax reads the settings your application already has.
When you do want to set something, every setting can come from several places.

## Where Migrax looks, in order

1. **Command line options**, such as `--url` or `--naming`.
2. **System properties**: `-Dmigrax.<key>`, set through `MIGRAX_JAVA_OPTS`.
3. **Environment variables**: `MIGRAX_<KEY>`, with dots and dashes turned into underscores.
4. **Application configuration**: `migrax.<key>` in your application's own files.
5. **Your framework's settings**, such as `spring.datasource.url`.

Application configuration files, from lowest to highest priority:

| File (in `src/main/resources`) | Used by |
|---|---|
| `META-INF/persistence.xml` (first persistence unit) | Jakarta EE, Helidon, plain Hibernate |
| `META-INF/microprofile-config.properties` | Helidon MP and other MicroProfile runtimes |
| `application.properties`, `application.yml`, `application.yaml` | Spring Boot, Quarkus, Micronaut, Helidon SE |
| `application-<profile>.*`, `microprofile-config-<profile>.properties` | the active profile |

The active profile comes from `MIGRAX_PROFILE`, `QUARKUS_PROFILE`, `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE`,
`MICRONAUT_ENVIRONMENTS` or `MP_CONFIG_PROFILE`, or the matching key in the configuration.
Several comma-separated profiles are loaded in order. `${VAR}` and `${VAR:default}` placeholders
in values are resolved from the environment.

## Settings

| Setting | Key / variable | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Database URL | `--url`, `MIGRAX_DATABASE_URL`, `migrax.url` | from the framework settings below |
| Database user | `--user`, `MIGRAX_DATABASE_USER`, `migrax.user` | from the framework settings |
| Database password | `--password`, `MIGRAX_DATABASE_PASSWORD`, `migrax.password` | from the framework settings |
| Secrets in files | `--password-file`, `MIGRAX_DATABASE_PASSWORD_FILE`, `MIGRAX_DATABASE_USER_FILE`, `MIGRAX_DATABASE_URL_FILE` | the file's content without its last line break; a value set directly wins |
| Lock timeout | `--lock-timeout`, `MIGRAX_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `-Dmigrax.lockTimeout`; `migrax.lock-timeout` in the startup integrations | `0` (fail at once); for example `30s`, `2m` |
| Drift check at startup | `migrax.drift.check` in the startup integrations | `off`; `warn` logs, `fail` stops the start ([details](../guides/production-safety.md#drift-at-startup)) |
| JDBC drivers without a project | `--classpath`, `MIGRAX_DRIVERS` (a folder of jars) | the `drivers` folder of the installation, if present |
| Never allow `clean` | `MIGRAX_CLEAN_DISABLED=true` | allowed |
| Entity package | `--package`, `MIGRAX_PACKAGE`, `migrax.package` | Maven `groupId` or Gradle `group` |
| Migration folders | `--locations`, `MIGRAX_LOCATIONS`, `migrax.locations` (comma-separated) | `classpath:db/migration` |
| Naming strategy | `--naming`, `MIGRAX_NAMING`, `migrax.naming` | recorded in the snapshot, else detected ([details](naming.md)) |
| Entity reader | `--extractor`, `MIGRAX_EXTRACTOR`, `migrax.extractor` | `auto` |
| Schema file (the desired schema as SQL, instead of entities; [guide](../guides/sql-migrations-for-any-language.md#let-migrax-write-the-migrations)) | `--schema-file`, `MIGRAX_SCHEMA_FILE`, `migrax.schema-file` | none: entities |
| Empty database to read the schema file in | `--scratch-url`, `MIGRAX_SCRATCH_URL`, `migrax.scratch-url` | a throwaway one (Docker for server databases) |
| Docker image for that throwaway database | `MIGRAX_SCRATCH_IMAGE`, `migrax.scratch-image` | as for `verify` |
| Check constraints for enum columns | `MIGRAX_ENUM_CHECKS`, `migrax.enum-checks` (`true` / `false`) | `false` ([details](../guides/changing-entities.md#enum-columns)) |
| SQL dialect | `--dialect` | from the database URL |
| Java migration package | `--java-package`, `migrax.java-package` | `db.migration` |
| Environment (`-- migrax:env` migrations) | `--env`, `MIGRAX_ENV`, `migrax.env` | none: marked migrations are skipped |
| Schemas (multi-tenant) | `--schemas`, `MIGRAX_SCHEMAS`, `migrax.schemas` | the connection's default schema |
| Placeholders | `migrax.placeholders.<name>`, `-Dmigrax.placeholders.<name>`, `MIGRAX_PLACEHOLDERS_<NAME>` | |
| Database to work on | `--database`, `MIGRAX_DATABASE`, `-Dmigrax.database` | the default database; others come from `migrax.databases.<name>.*` ([details](../guides/several-databases.md#the-command-line)) |
| Environments for `migrax environments` | `migrax.environments.<name>.url`, `.user`, `.password`, `.password-file`, `.env`; or `MIGRAX_ENVIRONMENTS_<NAME>_URL` and so on | none ([details](../guides/comparing-databases.md#all-environments-at-a-glance)) |
| Which environments, in which order | `--environments`, `MIGRAX_ENVIRONMENTS`, `migrax.environments` (comma-separated) | all configured, in alphabetical order |

Each migration folder is `classpath:<path>` (under `src/main/resources`) or
`filesystem:<path>` (relative to the project folder). A folder without a prefix, such as
`db/migration`, is a classpath folder, the same as when the application migrates at startup.
Several folders are separated by commas;
see [Several migration folders](../guides/advanced-migrations.md#several-migration-folders).

### Database connection from framework settings

| Framework | URL | User / password |
|---|---|---|
| Spring Boot | `spring.datasource.url`, `spring.datasource.hikari.jdbc-url`, `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL` | `spring.datasource.username` / `.password` |
| Quarkus | `quarkus.datasource.jdbc.url`, `QUARKUS_DATASOURCE_JDBC_URL` | `quarkus.datasource.username` / `.password` |
| Micronaut | `datasources.default.url` (or the first data source), `DATASOURCES_DEFAULT_URL` | `datasources.default.username` / `.password` |
| Helidon MP | `javax.sql.DataSource.<name>.dataSource.url` (or `jdbcUrl`, `URL`) | `...dataSource.user` / `...dataSource.password` |
| Helidon SE | `db.connection.url` | `db.connection.username` / `.password` |
| Jakarta EE | `jakarta.persistence.jdbc.url`, `javax.persistence.jdbc.url`, `hibernate.connection.url` | `...jdbc.user` / `...jdbc.password` |
| Any | `DATABASE_URL`, `DB_URL` | `DB_USERNAME` / `DB_PASSWORD` |

### Hibernate settings

Hibernate settings in `hibernate.*`, `spring.jpa.properties.*`, `jpa.default.properties.*`
(Micronaut), the naming-strategy keys of each framework, and `persistence.xml` properties are
passed to Hibernate when Migrax reads the mapping. Connection and schema-generation settings are
left out, because Migrax never connects Hibernate to your database while reading.

## The `.migrax` folder

| File | Commit? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot.json` | yes | Schema your migrations produce, with dialect and naming |
| `history/` | yes | Snapshot after each migration |
| `<name>/` | yes | `snapshot.json`, `history/` and `pending/` of a further database (`--database <name>`) |
| `classpath.txt`, `classpath.hash`, `build.stamp` | no | Build cache; refresh with `--refresh` |
| `.gitignore` | yes | Written by Migrax; ignores the caches |


---

Source: https://migrax.org/reference/naming/

# Naming strategies

Hibernate turns entity and field names into table and column names, and each framework
configures that differently. Migrax must use exactly the same rules, or the generated tables
won't be the ones your application looks for.

| Strategy | Used by | `homepageURL` | `fullName` | Join table for `Product.tags` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spring` | Spring Boot | `homepageurl` | `full_name` | `product_tags` |
| `jpa` | Quarkus, Helidon, Jakarta EE, plain Hibernate, Micronaut without Micronaut Data | `homepageURL` | `fullName` | `Product_Tag` |
| `micronaut` | Micronaut Data | `homepage_url` | `full_name` | `product_tag` |
| `jpa-snake` | Hibernate with only a snake_case physical strategy | `homepageurl` | `full_name` | `product_tag` |

Names you give explicitly with `@Table(name = ...)` or `@Column(name = ...)` pass through the
same physical rule: Spring Boot and Micronaut Data turn them into snake_case too.

## How Migrax chooses

1. An explicit setting: `--naming`, `MIGRAX_NAMING` or `migrax.naming`.
2. The naming recorded in `.migrax/snapshot.json` by the first `generate`. This keeps names
   stable even if the configuration changes later, for example when the database URL moves into
   environment variables.
3. A naming strategy configured for Hibernate, such as
   `spring.jpa.hibernate.naming.physical-strategy` or `hibernate.physical_naming_strategy`.
4. The framework's default, detected from the build file and configuration.

`migrax init` and `migrax doctor` show the result. When the snapshot's naming differs from what
your framework uses, `doctor` warns and explains how to switch.

!!! warning "Changing the naming of an existing project"

    Switching naming renames every affected column. Set `migrax.naming`, run `migrax generate`,
    and accept the renames it proposes, so the data is kept.

## Sequences

Generated ids (`@GeneratedValue` with `AUTO` or `SEQUENCE` and no named generator) use:

| Hibernate | Sequence |
|---|---|
| 6 and 7 | `<entity>_SEQ` per entity, allocation size 50 |
| 6 and 7 with Micronaut Data | one `hibernate_sequence` |
| 5.x | one `hibernate_sequence`, allocation size 1 |

On MySQL, which has no sequences, Hibernate uses a one-row `next_val` table of the same name,
and so does Migrax.


---

Source: https://migrax.org/reference/databases/

# Databases

| Database | Dialect name | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| PostgreSQL | `postgresql` | Transactional DDL; `generate --safe` for non-blocking indexes and constraints |
| CockroachDB | `cockroachdb` | Through the PostgreSQL driver; recognized from the server ([details](#cockroachdb)) |
| YugabyteDB 2024.2 and newer | `yugabytedb` | PostgreSQL's SQL; DDL commits immediately ([details](#yugabytedb)) |
| MySQL 8 | `mysql` | DDL commits immediately; sequences are `next_val` tables |
| MariaDB | `mariadb` | Like MySQL |
| TiDB 7.5 and newer | `tidb` | Through the MySQL driver; recognized from the server ([details](#tidb)) |
| SQL Server | `sqlserver` | Lock through `sp_getapplock` |
| Oracle 12c and newer | `oracle` | Lock needs `EXECUTE` on `DBMS_LOCK`; booleans follow the version ([details](#oracle)) |
| H2 | `h2` | For development and tests; `verify` uses it in memory |
| HSQLDB (HyperSQL) 2.7 and newer | `hsqldb` | In memory, files or server; `verify` uses it in memory ([details](#hsqldb)) |
| Apache Derby 10.16 and newer | `derby` | Embedded or network server; `verify` uses it in memory ([details](#derby)) |
| SQLite 3.35 and newer | `sqlite` | Changes SQLite can't make in place rebuild the table ([details](#sqlite)) |

The dialect comes from the JDBC URL. When there is no database URL (for example in a CI step that
only plans), pass `--dialect`.

## CockroachDB

CockroachDB speaks PostgreSQL's protocol, so the project uses the PostgreSQL driver and a
`jdbc:postgresql://host:26257/database` URL. Migrax asks the server which database it is, and
the first `generate` records `cockroachdb` in the snapshot, so later commands don't have to ask.
Without a reachable database, pass `--dialect cockroachdb`.

What is different from PostgreSQL:

- 32-bit integers are written as `int4`, because CockroachDB's `integer` has 64 bits.
- `@Lob` values are `text` and `bytea`: CockroachDB has no large objects.
- Indexes and unique constraints are removed with `DROP INDEX table@name`.
- The migration lock is a row in the `migrax_lock` table, because CockroachDB has no session
  locks. If a Migrax process is killed while migrating, the row stays and the next `migrate`
  says how to remove it.
- `verify` starts a throwaway `cockroachdb/cockroach` container in Docker.

CockroachDB widens a column in place (a longer `VARCHAR`, `INT4` to `INT8`). Any other type
change needs its experimental setting and can't run inside a transaction, so a migration with
one starts with `-- migrax:no-transaction` and
`SET enable_experimental_alter_column_type_general = true`. Its statements then commit one by
one: if one fails, the earlier ones stay applied.

## YugabyteDB

YugabyteDB (its YSQL API) runs PostgreSQL's own SQL layer, so Migrax writes the same SQL as for
PostgreSQL. Use the PostgreSQL driver with a `jdbc:postgresql://host:5433/database` URL, or
YugabyteDB's own driver (`jdbc:yugabytedb://`). With the PostgreSQL driver, Migrax asks the
server which database it is and the first `generate` records `yugabytedb` in the snapshot.
Without a reachable database, pass `--dialect yugabytedb`.

What is different from PostgreSQL:

- DDL commits immediately, as on MySQL: a migration that fails halfway leaves its earlier
  statements applied.
- The migration lock is PostgreSQL's advisory lock where YugabyteDB has it (2025.1 and newer).
  On older versions it is a row in the `migrax_lock` table, as on CockroachDB.
- There are no large objects, which Hibernate's PostgreSQL mapping uses for `@Lob`, so saving a
  `@Lob` value fails on YugabyteDB. Leave out `@Lob`: a `byte[]` field is then `bytea`, and a
  long `String` can be `@Column(columnDefinition = "text")`.
- `generate --safe` isn't needed: YugabyteDB builds indexes without blocking writes.
- `verify` starts a throwaway `yugabytedb/yugabyte` container in Docker (about a minute).

Zero-downtime changes (`generate --zero-downtime`) work as on PostgreSQL, with triggers for
renamed columns and views for renamed tables.

## TiDB

TiDB speaks MySQL's protocol, so the project uses the MySQL driver and a
`jdbc:mysql://host:4000/database` URL. Migrax asks the server which database it is, and the
first `generate` records `tidb` in the snapshot. Without a reachable database, pass
`--dialect tidb`. Migrax writes the SQL it writes for MySQL, as Hibernate's MySQL dialect maps
the entities for TiDB.

What is different from MySQL:

- Check constraints (`@Check`, and enum checks with `migrax.enum-checks`) are only kept with
  `SET GLOBAL tidb_enable_check_constraint = ON`; otherwise TiDB ignores them. `migrax doctor` warns when the entities have checks and the setting is off.
- `--keep-data` backs up dropped columns with `CREATE TABLE ... LIKE` and `INSERT ... SELECT`,
  because TiDB has no `CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT`.
- There are no triggers and no writable views, so `generate --zero-downtime` can't split
  column or table renames on TiDB. Drops, NOT NULL and type changes split as usual.
- There are no stored procedures.
- `verify` starts a throwaway `pingcap/tidb` container in Docker.

## HSQLDB

HyperSQL is recognized from `jdbc:hsqldb:` URLs, in memory (`jdbc:hsqldb:mem:`), in files or as
a server. `verify` replays the migrations on a new in-memory database, without Docker.

What is different from H2:

- DDL commits immediately, as on MySQL: a migration that fails halfway leaves its earlier
  statements applied.
- The migration lock is a row in the `migrax_lock` table, so two processes that share a file
  or server database don't migrate at once. If a Migrax process is killed while migrating, the
  row stays and the next `migrate` says how to remove it.
- Sequence ids have no column default (HyperSQL has no sequence default); Hibernate takes the
  next value from the sequence itself.
- Hibernate stores `Instant` as `timestamp` on HyperSQL. Projects read by annotation scanning
  (without a JPA provider) get `timestamp with time zone` for it, so prefer reading the
